To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SPL7 transcriptional network is a key regulator of Cu-dependent responses, that the Cu homeostasis is tightly controlled by a complex interplay of transcriptional and translational control, and that Cu-dependent activities play a major role in the dynamics of cell walls.
the plant cell wall is an important Cu accumulation site.
Cu is an essential cofactor for many proteins and is therefore required for the normal development of plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of Cu trafficking and its implication on cell wall dynamics.
the molecular mechanisms controlling the Cu homeostasis and the Cu-related activities in the cell wall.
the molecular mechanisms of Cu trafficking in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cu status in plants is tightly regulated, and that Cu is an important factor for cell wall dynamics.
Cu is a central player in the control of cell wall properties, and that this control is tightly linked to the Cu-dependent control of the plant cell cycle.
a Cu deficiency leads to a reduced primary production and Cu excess leads to a reduced cell wall strength, both with negative effects on plant survival and productivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a tight control over Cu homeostasis and trafficking is required for the plant to cope with the Cu excess that can be encountered in the soil, while Cu-dependent processes such as lignification are essential for plant survival.

Cu trafficking is a tightly controlled process in plants and its misbalance can have detrimental effects on plant development and productivity, as well as on the plant’s ability to respond to environmental cues.
Cu is a major player in cell wall dynamics, and the Cu-dependent activities of cell wall enzymes may be of major importance to the Cu-dependent responses in plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cu-dependent cell wall dynamics are a major determinant of Cu homeostasis in plants.
Cu homeostasis is not only essential for the maintenance of cellular functions, but also has a direct impact on the cell wall properties and the cell wall dynamics.
Cu is not a mere micronutrient, but rather an essential cofactor that is involved in the regulation of numerous cellular processes.
